title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to the 'équation des lacets' cycle, which continues La Longue Marche. In it Grothendieck studies how an arithmetic (Galois or Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type) automorphism, with cyclotomic value μ ∈ Ẑ*, acts on the profinite modular group. He looks for a matrix u ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) whose inner automorphism induces, on Sl(2,Ẑ)' (by passage to quotients), the given automorphism.

Conditions from the previous page:
- (66) det u = μ.
- (67) u σ∞ u^{-1} = ε' σ∞. Here σ∞ = [[0,1],[-1,0]] has order 4 and stabilises i.
- (68) u ρ u^{-1} = ε'' g ρ. Here ρ = [[0,1],[-1,1]] has order 6 (order 3 up to sign) and stabilises the point e^{iπ/3}; g is the 'cocycle' coming from the loop equation.
- Applying the norm map x ↦ x ρ(x) ρ²(x) gives ε'' = ε_2.
- Writing ε_2 g = α ρ(α)^{-1} gives (69): u = α u_0 with u_0 commuting with ρ.
- Hence u_0 = p + qρ = [[p,q],[-q,p+q]], an element of Ẑ[ρ] ≅ Ẑ ⊗ Z[ζ_3] (Eisenstein integers).

This page.
- (71) det u_0 = p² + pq + q², the norm form of Z[ζ_3].
- Since det α = δ = ε_3, condition (66) becomes (72): N(u_0) = p² + pq + q² = μ ε_3.
- Earlier relations (57), (58) give c² + cd + d² = ε_3/μ for auxiliary quantities (a,b,c,d). This suggested u_0 = μ(cρ + d), i.e. p = μd, q = μc, and it checks: N(μ(cρ+d)) = μ² · ε_3/μ = μ ε_3.
- Imposing (67) as well, he verified (73), but only in the case ε' = +1.
- He recalls that he first concluded ε' = +1 always. He then realised this conflicts with class field theory, and guessed that ε' = +1 iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4). This is exactly the splitting condition for p in Q(i).
- Eliminating (a,b,c,d) altogether, he reaches the 'disconcertingly simple' formula (74): u = μ(t σ∞ + u·1) = μ[[u,t],[-t,u]], with t² + u² = ε_2/μ (probably ⇔ ε_2 = 1).
- In (74) the matrix commutes with σ∞. It is μ times an element of Ẑ[i] ≅ Ẑ[σ∞] of norm 1/μ, so det = μ² · (1/μ) = μ.
- The next page checks [u,ρ] = g and then guesses the ε_2 = −1 case as an anti-similitude μ τ∞ (t σ∞ + u) involving the reflection τ∞.

Modern interpretation. The two elliptic points of M_{1,1} (j = 1728 with automorphism group μ_4 generated by σ∞, and j = 0 with μ_6 generated by ρ) carry CM elliptic curves with CM by Z[i] and Z[ζ_3]. A Galois element acts on their Tate modules by an element of (O_K ⊗ Ẑ)* of norm equal to the cyclotomic character when it fixes K (Hecke/CM theory). When it does not fix K it acts by an antilinear map, i.e. an anti-similitude composed with a reflection.
- The linear case corresponds to ε' = +1. The p ≡ 1 mod 4 guess is the statement that Frob_p acts linearly on the j = 1728 curve iff p splits in Q(i).
- The quantities ε_2 and ε_3 behave like the quadratic characters attached to Q(i) and Q(√−3).
- Grothendieck is thus rediscovering, in the loop-equation / profinite-SL2 language, the CM description of the local Galois action at the elliptic points.
errors: Notation clash in (74): the letter u denotes both the matrix (underlined on the next page) and the scalar coefficient. The margin note seems to flag exactly this.
The claim 'ε' always +1' was an admitted error, corrected on the page to the conjecture that ε' = +1 iff p ≡ 1 (4). This is consistent with the splitting of p in Q(i).
The equivalence '(74) ⇔ ε_2 = 1' is stated only as 'sans doute'. It is not proved here.
The derivation via (a,b,c,d) suffered 'erreurs de calcul', by his own account. The final formula is checked on the next page and is consistent: det = μ and it commutes with σ∞.

ideas.what: Lifting an arithmetic automorphism of the profinite modular group to an element u of GL2(Ẑ) with det u = μ that normalises the elliptic stabilisers σ∞ and ρ, up to sign.
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT action on π1 of M_{1,1} at the elliptic points; image of GT in the automorphisms of SL2(Ẑ)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions GT acting on the modular tower; details not published

ideas.what: Elements commuting with ρ (resp. σ∞) form Ẑ[ζ_3] (resp. Ẑ[i]); the determinant is the norm form p²+pq+q² (resp. t²+u²), and det u = μ becomes a norm equation N(u_0) = ±μ^{±1}.
ideas.modern_name: Commutants as orders of CM fields; Tate-module action of CM elliptic curves (Hecke character)

ideas.what: Sign ε' = +1 iff the automorphism fixes i (Frobenius: p ≡ 1 mod 4); otherwise u is an anti-similitude (reflection times similitude).
ideas.modern_name: Linear vs. antilinear Galois action on CM Tate modules; quadratic character of Q(i)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical class field theory / CM theory

ideas.what: Closed formula u = μ(t σ∞ + u), with t² + u² = 1/μ, satisfying the loop-equation commutator condition [u,ρ] = g.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit description of the local Galois/GT action at the j = 1728 elliptic point
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related explicit work by Nakamura and Ihara on Galois action at elliptic points (unsure of exact match)

missed.claim: Grothendieck connects the abstract loop-equation condition on SL2(Ẑ) lifts directly with class field theory of Q(i) and Q(√−3) at the elliptic points: the sign ε' is governed by p mod 4, and an anti-similitude appears in the non-split case. This is in effect a combinatorial rederivation of CM Galois action from the GT-type equations.
missed.quote: avant de m'apercevoir que ce n'était guère compatible avec le corps de classes, et de subodorer que l'on devait avoir ε' = +1 ssi p ≡ 1 (4)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests that the GT relations alone force the CM structure at the elliptic points. This is a known circle of ideas (Nakamura, Ihara), but Grothendieck's explicit matrix normal form with the ε_2/ε_3 sign bookkeeping may be a useful independent derivation.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit, unpublished computation linking the loop-equation formalism to CM class field theory at the elliptic points. The underlying mathematics (CM action, Galois action on π1 of M_{1,1}) is known from later work by Ihara, Nakamura and others, so the novelty is mainly historical and in the explicit normal form.
transcription_corrections: 'mais en un plus-x dans le cas ε'=+1 exclusivement' should most likely read 'mais en me plaçant dans le cas ε' = +1 exclusivement'.
In the (57 et 58) relation, read c² + cd + d² = ε_3/μ.
(74) should be written with an underlined matrix: u̲ = μ(t σ∞ + u) = μ[[u,t],[−t,u]], with the side note '(⇔ sans doute, ε_2 = 1)'.
'correspond manifestement au cas ε'_1 = 1' is probably simply ε' = 1.
The margin note is roughly: 'Je souligne la lettre u qui désigne une matrice dans (74), pour la distinguer de la lettre u [scalaire]…', i.e. a note on the notation clash; partly illegible.
